info.title: AI Stylist API
info.description:
Public API of the AI Stylist backend. URI-versioned (`/v1`); changes within `v1` are additive.
Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable machine `code` from
`@ai-stylist/shared-kernel`.

tags.name: platform
tags.description: Health, version and other non-domain endpoints

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Sign-in, sessions, account recovery, consent, data export and account deletion

tags.name: profile
tags.description: Profile settings, body measurements, style preferences and onboarding progress

get.description: Returns `ok` when the API and every checked dependency are reachable.

503.description: One or more dependencies are down

get.summary: Build identity of the running API
get.description: Semantic version, commit SHA and build timestamp of the deployed API.

post.summary: Sign in with an Apple or Google identity token
post.description:
The app runs the provider's native sign-in and sends the identity token it received.
The server verifies the token with the provider's keys, then answers with one
`SignInResult`: a session for an existing account, `sign_up_required` for an identity
with no account (nothing is stored until `completeSignUp` accepts the birth year), or
`deletion_pending` for an account inside its deletion grace window (no session). No
provider token is ever returned.

post.summary: Complete a pending sign-up with the self-declared birth year (age gate)
post.description:
Second part of a sign-up. The first part is a sign-in whose answer was
`sign_up_required`; the `signUpToken` of that answer authorizes this call. The server
applies the age gate (16+, DEC-60) to the birth year. Accepted: the account is created
and the answer is the `session` outcome. Refused: `AGE_GATE_FAILED`, nothing about the
attempt is stored, and the sign-up token is spent; a new attempt starts again with a
sign-in. Identity's own operation: better-auth 1.7.12 has no path for it.

401.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the sign-up token is missing, expired, already spent or unknown. Start again with a sign-in.

403.description:
`AGE_GATE_FAILED`: the birth year lies fewer than 16 years back (DEC-60). Terminal
for this attempt: nothing is stored and the sign-up token is spent. The client shows
its refusal screen and offers no way to change the year.

get.summary: WebAuthn options for a passkey sign-in
get.description:
Returns a fresh challenge and the WebAuthn request options (W3C WebAuthn
`PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON`) for the platform passkey API. Without a session
no credentials are listed, so the device offers its discoverable passkeys.

post.summary: Sign in with a passkey assertion
post.description:
Verifies the assertion the platform passkey API returned for the challenge of
`getPasskeySignInOptions`. Answers `session`, or `deletion_pending` for an account inside
its deletion grace window. A passkey always belongs to an existing account, so this
operation never answers `sign_up_required`.

get.summary: WebAuthn options to add a passkey to the signed-in account
get.description:
Returns a fresh challenge and the WebAuthn creation options (W3C WebAuthn
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`). The account's existing passkeys are listed as
excluded credentials. Needs a recently created session (better-auth `freshAge`);
otherwise 403 `FORBIDDEN`, and the client signs in again first.

post.summary: Add a passkey to the signed-in account
post.description:
Verifies the attestation the platform passkey API returned for the challenge of
`getPasskeyRegistrationOptions` and stores the passkey on the caller's account. An
account may hold several passkeys. Opens no new session.

get.description:
The account and expiry of the session the bearer token belongs to. Read-only: it does
not extend the session (better-auth `deferSessionRefresh`). A token with no live session
is answered with 401, never with an empty body.

post.description:
Extends the session the bearer token belongs to and answers with its token and new
expiry. The answer may carry a different token than the one presented: the client
stores the returned token and discards the old one. A 401 here is a refused renewal:
the client ends the session on the device and sends no further call for it.
Revokes the session the bearer token belongs to on the server.

get.summary: List the signed-in devices of the caller
get.description:
One entry per active session of the caller's account (the device list, doc 11 §4.2),
newest first, cursor-paginated (doc 06 §2). Never another user's sessions and never a
session token.

200.description: One page of the caller's sessions

post.description: Revokes every session of the caller's account, the current one included.

200.description: Every session of the account is revoked

post.summary: Ask for an account-recovery link by email
post.description:
Fallback for a person who lost their passkeys (doc 11 §15). The answer is the same
status and body whether or not an account exists for the address, so it discloses
nothing. When one exists, a single-use link is emailed; it works from 24 to 48 hours
after the request, and any signed-in session of the account can cancel it before then
(`cancelAccountRecovery`). Never creates an account.

get.description:
Exchanges the token of a recovery link for a sign-in. Refused before 24 hours and from
48 hours after the request, after a cancel, and on a second use. The person then adds
a new passkey with `registerPasskey`. The server never logs the query string of this
path.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Single-use token from the emailed link.

401.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the link is unknown, used, cancelled, not yet valid or expired.

delete.description:
Cancels the pending recovery link of the caller's account during its 24-hour delay.
Only a signed-in session of that account can cancel; holding the mailbox is not
enough. Identity's own operation: better-auth 1.7.12 has no path for it.

204.description: The pending recovery is cancelled; its link no longer works.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the account has no pending recovery.

get.summary: The caller's current consent per purpose
get.description:
The latest consent record of each purpose the caller has decided on, cursor-paginated.
A purpose with no record is absent and its default applies (doc 11 §7.2). The full
append-only history is part of the data export.

200.description: One page of current consent records

post.summary: Grant or withdraw consent for one purpose
post.description:
Appends a consent record for one purpose (doc 11 §7.1; append-only: a withdrawal is a
new record). 201 when a record was appended. 200 when the request repeats the current
state for the same policy version: nothing is stored and the current record, with its
original dates, is returned.

403.description:
`CONSENT_REQUIRED`: a withdrawal of `core_service` is refused. This consent is
required to use the app (doc 11 §7.2). Deleting the account is what ends this
processing (`POST /v1/me/deletion`).

post.summary: Request an export of the caller's data
post.description:
Starts an asynchronous export of the caller's data (doc 11 §13.1), open on every plan
(`data.export`). Answers at once with the new export `in_progress`; the client reads it
with `getDataExport` until it is `ready` (a notification follows as well). One export
runs at a time per account: while one is in progress, a new request is refused with 429
and the running export.

202.description: The export is accepted and in progress

get.summary: Read one of the caller's data exports
get.description:
The state of an export. While it is `ready`, every read mints a new download link after
the same authorization check; the link lives at most 10 minutes (DEC-44, doc 11 §5.4).
The archive itself is kept until `availableUntil`. Never cached.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the caller has no export with this id.

post.summary: Request deletion of the caller's account
post.description:
Starts the deletion of the caller's account (doc 11 §13.2). At once every session of the
account is revoked, this one included, and a sign-in opens no session; the account is
kept for a 7-day grace window (DEC-65). A sign-in during the window answers
`deletion_pending`, whose cancel credential can stop the deletion
(`cancelAccountDeletion`). After the window the purge runs and cannot be stopped.
Re-authentication (doc 02 §11.3): needs a recently created session (better-auth
`freshAge`); otherwise 403 `FORBIDDEN`, and the client signs in again first. After the
answer the token of this request no longer works and the client returns to its
signed-out start. Deleting the account does not cancel a store subscription.

202.description: The deletion is requested; its grace window has started

403.description:
`FORBIDDEN`: the session was not created recently enough to confirm it is the person.
The client signs in again with the same account and repeats the request.

429.description:
`RATE_LIMITED`: the account requested a deletion within the last 30 days (doc 11
§14), or another rate limit was hit; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

delete.summary: Cancel the account deletion inside its grace window
delete.description:
Stops a pending account deletion during its 7-day grace window (DEC-65). The only
credential accepted is the cancel credential of the `deletion_pending` sign-in outcome
(`deletionCancelToken`); the caller holds no session, because the deletion revoked them
all. The account is active again, but no session is opened or restored: the client signs
in again. Once the window has ended the cancel is refused with 410 `ACCOUNT_DELETED`.

204.description: The deletion is cancelled and the account is active; sign in to open a session.

401.description:
`UNAUTHENTICATED`: the cancel credential is missing, malformed or expired. The client
signs in again; during the window that sign-in answers `deletion_pending` with a new
credential.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the account has no pending deletion, e.g. it was already cancelled.

410.description:
`ACCOUNT_DELETED`: the grace window has ended, so the deletion can no longer be
cancelled; the account is deleted or being purged. The client erases everything it
stores for the account and returns to its signed-out start. Not cached.

get.description:
Presentation, starting shape and the six settings of REQ-ONB-100. A profile nothing has
been written to answers with its defaults and `version` 0.

patch.summary: Change some of the caller's profile settings
patch.description:
Partial update (see the file header): each member present replaces its stored value.
Answers with the whole profile at its new `version`.

400.description:
`VALIDATION_FAILED`: the body breaks this schema, or `startingShape` is not a shape
of the shared-kernel registry. `errors[]` names each field.

get.description:
The caller's current measurement set, in SI units. A set nothing has been written to
answers with no measurement and `version` 0. Never cached.

400.description:
`MEASUREMENT_IMPLAUSIBLE`: a value lies outside its hard bounds (shared-kernel
`registry/measurement-definitions.json`, doc 07 §3.3). Nothing of the request is
stored. `errors[]` points at each refused value (e.g. `/measurements/height/value`)
and never repeats it (doc 11 §8). `VALIDATION_FAILED`: the body breaks this schema,
e.g. an estimated or derived value without `confidence`.

get.description:
Fit and style preferences, soft dislikes and hard exclusions, climate tolerance,
occasions and the typical day, and usual sizes. Preferences nothing has been written to
answer with empty lists and `version` 0.

patch.summary: Change some of the caller's style preferences
patch.description:
Partial update (see the file header): each member present replaces its stored value
whole, an empty list or object empties it, and `clear` removes `climateTolerance` or
`typicalDay`. Answers with all preferences at their new `version`.

400.description:
`VALIDATION_FAILED`: the body breaks this schema, a member is both set and named in
`clear`, or `sizingByRegion` holds two entries for one size system and garment group.
`errors[]` names each field.

get.description:
Per-step progress of the onboarding flow (doc 02 §3.2) and the step the app resumes at
after a quit or a crash.

patch.summary: Record the outcome of onboarding steps
patch.description:
Records `completed` or `skipped` for each step present. A status only moves forward
(`pending` → `skipped` → `completed`): a write that would move a step back leaves it
unchanged and is still answered with 200, so a replayed or late write from a device's
local buffer is harmless. Answers with the whole progress.

400.description:
`VALIDATION_FAILED`: the body breaks this schema, or it marks a required step
`skipped`. `errors[]` names each step.

get.description:
The entitlements the server resolves for the caller now (doc 12 §3.2): over the caller's
active grants the most generous value wins, per entitlement; an entitlement no active
grant supplies takes its Free-plan value (doc 12 §1.2). Every registered entitlement
appears once. The apps may cache the answer briefly to render (doc 12 §3.3); a gated
request is decided by the server alone.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details (planning/06 §2). `code` is stable and machine-readable.

code.description: Stable machine code from the shared-kernel error registry

errors.description: Field-level validation failures with JSON-pointer paths

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the request body

version.description: Semantic version of the deployed API

commit.description: Git commit SHA the build was produced from

IdentityProvider.description: Identity providers that sign in with a native identity token (DEC-64).

token.description: The provider's identity token (a JWT), verified against the provider's keys.

nonce.description:
The unhashed nonce the app generated for the provider request. The identity
token's `nonce` claim must equal it or its SHA-256 digest. Sign in with Apple
requires it.

user.description: Name the provider reports to the app on the first authorization only (Sign in with Apple).

UserId.description: Account id, a prefixed ULID (`usr_`, shared-kernel `ID_PREFIXES.user`).

SessionGrant.description: A session the server opened or renewed.

token.description: The session token for `bearerAuth`. Kept in the Keychain or Keystore-backed storage only (doc 11 §4.2).

expiresAt.description:
When the session ends unless renewed with `refreshSession`. The server may refuse
the token earlier (revocation, or a shorter access window, doc 11 §4.2); the client
then renews once.

DeletionPending.description:
The account is inside its 7-day deletion grace window (DEC-65): no session was opened.
The only thing the client can do is offer to cancel the deletion with `cancelToken`.

graceEndsAt.description: End of the grace window; the purge starts after it.

cancelToken.description: Value for the `Deletion-Cancel-Token` header (`deletionCancelToken`); valid only for `DELETE /v1/me/deletion`.

SignUpPending.description:
The verified identity has no account. Nothing is stored. The client asks for the birth
year and calls `completeSignUp` with `token`.

token.description:
Sign-up credential for `CompleteSignUpRequest.signUpToken`. Single use, valid only
for `completeSignUp`; it opens no session and grants nothing else.

SignInResult.description:
One sign-in outcome. `outcome` names it, and exactly the object of that outcome is
present: `session` for `session`, `deletionPending` for `deletion_pending`, `signUp` for
`sign_up_required`. Only `session` opens a session.

birthYear.description:
Self-declared birth year (DEC-60). Only a sanity range is enforced here; the age
floor is the server's rule and is never restated by a client.

Base64Url.description: Base64url without padding (RFC 4648 §5), as WebAuthn JSON encodes binary values.

PasskeyExtensionInputs.description:
WebAuthn extension inputs (`AuthenticationExtensionsClientInputsJSON`). Only the
extensions this API requests are modelled.

PasskeyExtensionOutputs.description:
WebAuthn extension outputs (`AuthenticationExtensionsClientOutputsJSON`). Only the
extensions this API reads are modelled; send `{}` when there are none.

name.description: Label the person gives the passkey.

PasskeySummary.description: A passkey stored on the account. Carries no key material.

SessionInfo.description: The current session, without its token.

needsRefresh.description: True when the server asks the client to renew now with `refreshSession`.

DeviceSession.description: One signed-in device of the caller. Carries no token and no IP address.

current.description: True for the session that made this request.

userAgent.description: The `User-Agent` the device sent at sign-in, to tell devices apart.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

status.description: Always true, whether or not an account exists for the address.

ConsentRecordId.description: Consent record id, a prefixed ULID (`cns_`, shared-kernel `ID_PREFIXES.consentRecord`).

ConsentPurpose.description:
Consent purpose keys of doc 11 §7.2, in that order. Mirrors shared-kernel
`CONSENT_PURPOSES` value for value (pinned by packages/contracts/tests/kernel-enums.test.ts).

PolicyVersion.description: Version of the policy text the person saw, e.g. `0.1.0-draft`.

ConsentSurface.description: Identifier of the app screen where the decision was made, e.g. `onboarding_consent`.

ConsentRecord.description:
One append-only consent record (doc 11 §7.1); `locale` is the language of the text the
person saw.

grantedAt.description: When the consent was granted; present when `status` is `granted`.

withdrawnAt.description: When the consent was withdrawn; present when `status` is `withdrawn`.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

ConsentChange.description: One consent decision; `locale` is the language of the text the person saw.

DataExportId.description: Data-export id, a prefixed ULID (`xpt_`, shared-kernel `ID_PREFIXES.exportRequest`).

DataExportStatus.description:
`in_progress` until the archive is built; then `ready` until `availableUntil`, when the
archive is deleted and the export becomes `expired`. `failed` when it could not be
built: nothing is kept, and the person may request a new export.

DataExportDownload.description: Present only while the export is `ready`. Minted for this response; never stored by the server.

url.description:
Presigned GET of the archive, minted after the same authorization check as the
export (doc 11 §13.1). It carries a live signature: never log, share or store it
(doc 11 §8). Read the export again for a fresh link.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops working, at most 10 minutes after it was minted (DEC-44, doc 11 §5.4).

DataExport.description:
One data export of the caller (doc 11 §13.1): a ZIP archive of the caller's data in
machine-readable JSON plus the media they uploaded. This object never carries archive
content.

readyAt.description: When the archive was built; present for `ready` and `expired`.

availableUntil.description:
When the archive is deleted, 24 hours after `readyAt` (doc 11 §13.1); present for
`ready` and `expired`. This is how long the archive is kept, not how long a link
works: every read of a `ready` export mints a new link.

DataExportInProgress.description: A problem (RFC 9457) that carries the running export when an export is already in progress.

AccountDeletionRequestId.description: Account-deletion request id, a prefixed ULID (`del_`, shared-kernel `ID_PREFIXES.deletionRequest`).

graceEndsAt.description:
End of the 7-day grace window (DEC-65). Until then a sign-in offers to cancel the
deletion; after it the purge runs, and a cancel is refused with 410 `ACCOUNT_DELETED`.

ProfileId.description: Profile id, a prefixed ULID (`prf_`, shared-kernel `ID_PREFIXES.profile`).

ResourceVersion.description:
Version of the resource (doc 06 §2). It grows by one with every accepted write; 0 means
nothing has been written yet. Send it back as `If-Match: "<version>"`.

Presentation.description:
Presentation the person chooses (doc 03 §1.2, doc 07 §3.1); never inferred, and it never
limits which starting shape or measurements are valid. Default `unspecified`. Mirrors
shared-kernel `PRESENTATIONS`.

StartingShapeId.description:
Id of the starting shape the avatar begins from (doc 07 §3.1), the base-model selection
of onboarding. One of the shapes of the shared-kernel registry
`registry/starting-shapes.json`; the server refuses any other id with 400
`VALIDATION_FAILED`. Default `from_measurements`. An id string, not an enum, so that a
shape can be added or retired (P04) without a breaking contract change. The base mesh
all shapes share is a kernel constant and is not stored per person.

UnitSystem.description:
How the apps show measurements; it never changes what the API stores or returns (SI).
Mirrors shared-kernel `UNIT_SYSTEMS`.

RegionCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code, e.g. `DE`. A setting the person chooses, not a location.

AccessibilitySettings.description: Accessibility settings the apps apply (phase P03 §4). Both are `false` by default.

reducedMotion.description: Show no motion that is not needed to understand the screen.

prefersNon3d.description: Prefer flat images to 3D views wherever the app offers both.

Profile.description:
The caller's profile settings. `presentation` and `startingShape` are independent: any
presentation goes with any starting shape (REQ-ONB-050). The six settings of REQ-ONB-100
are `locale` (formats dates and numbers, e.g. `en-GB`), `language` (the language of the
app's text, e.g. `en`), `unitSystem`, `timezone`, `region` and `accessibility`. The first
five are absent until the person confirms them in onboarding (step "units and locale";
the app pre-fills them from the device), and are edited, not removed, after that.

ProfileUpdate.description:
Partial update of `Profile`: each member present replaces its stored value. `presentation`
returns to its default by sending `unspecified`, `startingShape` by sending
`from_measurements`.

ProfileVersionConflict.description: A problem (RFC 9457) that carries the stored profile when `code` is `VERSION_MISMATCH`.

MeasurementSource.description:
Who produced the value (doc 06 §3.1): the person (`user`), an estimate, or a value
derived from other values. Mirrors shared-kernel `MEASUREMENT_SOURCES`.

MeasurementConfidence.description: Confidence in the value, from 0 to 1.

LengthMeasurement.description:
A body length in centimetres with its provenance (doc 06 §3.1). `confidence` is always
present when `source` is `estimated` or `derived`, and optional for `user`.

measuredAt.description: When the value was taken or entered.

MassMeasurement.description:
A body mass in kilograms with its provenance (doc 06 §3.1). `confidence` is always
present when `source` is `estimated` or `derived`, and optional for `user`.

measuredAt.description: When the value was taken or entered.

BodyMeasurements.description:
The ten body measurements of doc 07 §3.3, each optional: an absent one has not been
given. Their ids, units and hard bounds are shared-kernel registry data
(`registry/measurement-definitions.json`); a value outside its bounds is refused with
400 `MEASUREMENT_IMPLAUSIBLE` and never stored.

MeasurementSet.description:
The caller's current measurement set (doc 03 §1.2). Each value is SI with its unit and
source; `unitSystem` changes only how an app shows it.

MeasurementsReplacement.description: The whole new measurement set; a measurement left out is removed.

MeasurementSetVersionConflict.description: A problem (RFC 9457) that carries the stored measurement set when `code` is `VERSION_MISMATCH`.

FitPreferences.description:
Preferred fit per garment group (doc 08 §4.2 `attr.cut`); a group with no choice is
absent. The keys are the shared-kernel `GARMENT_GROUPS` except `shoes`.

StyleTypeList.description: The style types the person selected (style identity, doc 03 §1.2).

Material.description: Material values of doc 08 §4.1 `attr.material`. Mirrors shared-kernel `MATERIALS`.

PreferenceItem.description:
One soft dislike or hard exclusion. `kind` names the list `value` comes from; the only
kind is `material`.

ClimateTolerance.description: How warm or cold the person usually feels (REQ-ONB-070). Mirrors shared-kernel `CLIMATE_TOLERANCES`.

OccasionPreset.description:
Occasion presets (doc 03 §1.7). As `typicalDay`, the occasion suggestions use whenever
the person selects none (DEC-71). Mirrors shared-kernel `OCCASION_PRESETS`.

OccasionPresetList.description: The occasions the person selected in onboarding.

UsualSize.description: A usual label size in one size system for one garment group (doc 08 §5).

size.description: The label size as written, e.g. `39`, `M` or `10.5`.

UsualSizeList.description:
The person's usual label sizes, at most one per size system and garment group (one entry
for each pair of `SizeSystem` and `GarmentGroup`). No size per brand.

Preferences.description:
The caller's style preferences. Hard exclusions are never broken by a suggestion; soft
dislikes only lower a score (REQ-ONB-060, doc 03 §1.2). An unset `climateTolerance`
counts as `neutral`.

ClearablePreference.description: A `Preferences` member that holds one optional value and can be removed.

PreferencesUpdate.description:
Partial update of `Preferences`: each member present replaces its stored value whole. A
member may not be both set and named in `clear`.

PreferencesVersionConflict.description: A problem (RFC 9457) that carries the stored preferences when `code` is `VERSION_MISMATCH`.

OnboardingStepStatus.description: `pending` until the person completes or skips the step; it never returns to `pending`.

required.description: True when onboarding cannot finish without this step; only optional steps offer Skip.

OnboardingSteps.description:
One entry per onboarding step, keyed by step; the keys are the `OnboardingStep` values in
camelCase. `signIn` is completed by the server when the account is created.

OnboardingStep.description: Onboarding steps of doc 02 §3.2, in flow order.

OnboardingProgress.description:
Per-step onboarding progress (doc 02 §3.2), kept on the server so the app resumes after
a quit or a crash. `nextRequiredStep` is the first required step not yet completed; the
app resumes there, and opens Today when it is absent.

OnboardingStepOutcome.description: `skipped` is refused for a required step.

OnboardingStepsUpdate.description: The outcome of each step present; an absent step is left unchanged.

EntitlementLifecycleState.description:
Lifecycle state of the caller's entitlements (doc 03 §4.3): the server-granted trial,
Free, a paid subscription, its billing-retry grace period, or a cancelled subscription
still paid until its period ends. Mirrors shared-kernel `ENTITLEMENT_LIFECYCLE_STATES`.

EntitlementName.description:
Entitlement names (doc 12 §3.1), in registry order. Mirrors the keys of shared-kernel
`ENTITLEMENTS` value for value; the apps read each name's kind and levels from the
generated kernel.

EntitlementGrantKind.description:
The kind of grant that supplied the value (doc 12 §3.2): the subscription's plan, the
3-day trial (doc 12 §2), a promotion, or a capability kept from an older plan version
(doc 12 §5.5). Absent from a `ResolvedEntitlement` when no active grant supplies the
entitlement and its Free-plan value applies. Mirrors shared-kernel
`ENTITLEMENT_GRANT_KINDS`.

EntitlementLevel.description:
One of the levels the shared-kernel registry lists for the entitlement
(`registry/entitlements.json`, `levels`, lowest first), e.g. `G2` for
`tryon.generative`. A string, not an enum, because each level entitlement has levels of
its own.

ResolvedEntitlement.description:
The resolved value of one entitlement. The value member present follows the kind of
`name` in the shared-kernel registry (`registry/entitlements.json`): `boolean` →
`granted`, always present; `limit` → `limit`, always present; `level` → `level`, absent
when no level is granted; `map` (`credits.weights`) → none yet, the weights join with the
credit ledger (P13).

granted.description: `boolean` kind: whether the capability is available.

limit.description:
`limit` kind: the cap, e.g. closet items or recommendations per local day. `null`
means unlimited (doc 06 §3.6).

EntitlementState.description:
The caller's entitlement state (doc 06 §3.6; semantics doc 12 §2–§3). `state` is the
lifecycle state of doc 03 §4.3. Generative credits (doc 12 §4) join this object with the
credit ledger (P13).

stateEndsAt.description:
When `state` ends unless something changes: the end of the trial for `trial`, the end
of paid access for `grace` and `cancelled_active`. Absent for `free` and `active_paid`,
which do not end on their own.

entitlements.description: One entry per registered entitlement, in shared-kernel registry order.

SignInRefused.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the identity token or passkey assertion was not accepted.

RateLimited.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: a rate limit was hit (doc 11 §14); retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

Unauthenticated.description:
`UNAUTHENTICATED`: the credential is missing, malformed, expired or revoked. The client
renews the session once (`refreshSession`); if the renewal is refused too, it signs in
again.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is authenticated but may not perform this operation. `code` is `FORBIDDEN`
unless the operation names a more specific code for this status.

AccountDeleted.description:
`ACCOUNT_DELETED`: the account is deleted or its deletion is in progress. The client
erases everything it stores for the account and returns to its signed-out start; it
tells this reply from 401 by the status alone. A 410 is cacheable by default
(RFC 9110 §15.5.11), so the reply carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and must not be
cached.

DataExportLimited.description:
`RATE_LIMITED`: an export of this account is already in progress, and `current` is that
export (read it with `getDataExport`); or another rate limit was hit, without `current`.
Retry after `Retry-After` seconds (doc 11 §14).

ProfileConflict.description:
`VERSION_MISMATCH`: `If-Match` names an older version than the stored one. `current` is
the stored profile, so the app can keep the losing edit and offer to re-apply it on top
(doc 04 §8). `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` or `CONFLICT` otherwise, without `current`.

MeasurementSetConflict.description:
`VERSION_MISMATCH`: `If-Match` names an older version than the stored one. `current` is
the stored measurement set, so the app can keep the losing edit and offer to re-apply it
on top (doc 04 §8). `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` or `CONFLICT` otherwise, without `current`.

PreferencesConflict.description:
`VERSION_MISMATCH`: `If-Match` names an older version than the stored one. `current` is
the stored preferences, so the app can keep the losing edit and offer to re-apply it on
top (doc 04 §8). `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` or `CONFLICT` otherwise, without `current`.

bearerAuth.description:
Session token issued by a sign-in (`SessionGrant.token`), sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (doc 06 §2). Opaque to clients: never parse it. A
missing, malformed, expired or revoked token is answered with the `Unauthenticated`
(401) problem. The client then renews once with `refreshSession`; a refused renewal
ends the session on the device.

deletionCancelToken.name: Deletion-Cancel-Token
deletionCancelToken.description:
Cancel credential of the `deletion_pending` sign-in outcome
(`DeletionPending.cancelToken`), sent in the `Deletion-Cancel-Token` header. Its only
use is `DELETE /v1/me/deletion`, the cancel of an account deletion inside its 7-day
grace window (DEC-65); every other operation refuses it. Single purpose, and valid for
at most 15 minutes from issue, no longer than an access token (doc 11 §4.2); the exact
expiry is `DeletionPending.cancelTokenExpiresAt`. It opens no session. A header of its
own, not `Authorization`, so it can never be taken for a session token.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated ULID that makes a mutating request safe to retry (doc 06 §2; the
mobile mutation-log `opId`). The server keeps key, request hash and response for 48 h:
a replay with the same body returns the stored response, the same key with a different
body is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Optional for the caller.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the `nextCursor` of the previous page; omit for the first page.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
The `version` of the resource the client last read, as a quoted integer, e.g. `"3"`
(doc 06 §2). Every write to a versioned resource sends it; a stale version is refused
with 409 `VERSION_MISMATCH`.

CacheControlNoStore.description: Always `no-store`; the response must not be stored by any cache.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (RFC 9110 §10.2.3, delay-seconds form).
